stem.text: A student separated the pigments in a plant leaf using paper chromatography. The student analysed the positions of the separated pigments to identify the pigments.
Figure 4.1 shows the chromatogram results and analysis.

stem.caption: Figure 4.1
stem.alt: Paper chromatogram of leaf pigments, with Rf values and pigment identities.

stem.text: The student was provided with a prepared extract containing the leaf pigments.
Outline how the student obtained the results shown in Figure 4.1 and analysed them to deduce the names of the pigments present.

(named) solvent below, extract / line, and idea of time to rise / left till solvent rises / wait till solvent almost reaches top ;
remove paper (before solvent reaches end) and mark solvent front ;
(Rf =) distance pigment moved ÷ distance solvent moved ;
check / compare with, known / reference / published, data / values ;

explanation.text: A pigment’s Rf is its travel distance from the origin divided by the solvent-front distance from the same origin. Keep the initial pigment spot above the solvent so that it is carried along the paper rather than dissolving into the reservoir.

reasoningChain: Apply extract to the pencil origin and let solvent rise.
Mark the solvent front, calculate Rf and compare with reference values.
